marker: nhé / nha / nhá ở cuối câu
what_it_carries: The speaker is asking rather than instructing, and expects the reader to go along with it
translated_instead: A bare imperative, or `Vui lòng` bolted on the front of one
example_human: Để mình gói riêng phần đá nha.
example_translated: Vui lòng giữ phần đá riêng biệt.
wrong_when: pr; sales-deck; a legal notice - a particle aimed at one reader is out of register there

marker: đấy / cơ / kia ở cuối câu
what_it_carries: Corrects an expectation the reader is already holding, without naming it
translated_instead: An adversative connective at the front of the sentence, usually `Thực tế là`
example_human: Rang hôm qua thôi đấy.
example_translated: Thực tế là sản phẩm được rang từ ngày hôm qua.
wrong_when: pr; sales-deck - correcting an unstated assumption reads as arguing with the reader

marker: thôi / mà / chứ ở cuối câu
gloss_en: final particle marking the claim as already agreed
what_it_carries: Treats the claim as obvious, or as settled between the two of you
translated_instead: A hedge in front of the claim, which does the opposite job
example_human: Bán hết là đóng cửa thôi.
example_translated: Cửa hàng sẽ đóng khi sản phẩm được bán hết.
wrong_when: sales-deck; pr - `thôi` shrinks the one claim the document exists to make

marker: ạ / hả / à ở cuối câu
gloss_en: final particle carrying deference or a question back
what_it_carries: Places the speaker relative to the reader: ạ defers, hả asks back
translated_instead: `Có phải…?` or `Xin cho biết…`, an interrogative frame with no stance in it
example_human: Quán mở tới mấy giờ ạ?
example_translated: Xin cho biết thời gian đóng cửa của quán.
wrong_when: Any surface where the brand is not a person - ạ from a company account reads as staff on the wrong login

marker: Chủ đề đứng trước, `thì` nối sang phần bình luận
what_it_carries: Names what the sentence is about before saying anything about it, which is how Vietnamese orders information
translated_instead: Subject-verb-object in English order, because the English sentence was the unit being translated
example_human: Tiền vận chuyển thì shop chịu.
example_translated: Shop sẽ chịu chi phí vận chuyển.
wrong_when: A spec table or a price list, where there is no comment to make about the topic

marker: Loại từ cộng này / đó / ấy / kia
what_it_carries: Points at one physical thing near the reader instead of naming a category
translated_instead: A bare noun, because English put an article there and the article does not survive the crossing
example_human: Cái tô đó nặng hơn tô thường.
example_translated: Sản phẩm có khối lượng lớn hơn mức tiêu chuẩn.
wrong_when: A catalogue line - the reader is not standing in front of the thing, so there is no đó to point with

marker: Động từ chính dán liền ra / vào / lên / xuống / qua / về
gloss_en: main verb followed directly by a direction verb
what_it_carries: Keeps the movement inside the verb, where Vietnamese keeps it
translated_instead: A prepositional phrase after the verb, copied off the English word order
example_human: Nhân viên xách ra tận xe.
example_translated: Nhân viên sẽ vận chuyển đến phương tiện của khách.
wrong_when: Nothing in the sentence physically moves

marker: rồi / luôn đóng câu
what_it_carries: Marks where the event sits relative to now, which Vietnamese does with an adverb and English does with tense
translated_instead: `đã được` plus the verb - an English tense rendered as a Vietnamese morpheme
example_human: Ba giờ chiều là hết rồi.
example_translated: Sản phẩm đã được bán hết vào lúc 15 giờ.
wrong_when: A specification, where the reader needs the state and not the speaker's relation to it

marker: Câu hỏi kết bằng không / chưa / hả
gloss_en: question closed on a final particle
what_it_carries: Asks the way a person asks, with the question mark falling on the last word
translated_instead: `Có phải…?` or `Liệu…?`, an English interrogative frame lifted whole
example_human: Còn size M không?
example_translated: Xin cho biết sản phẩm có còn kích cỡ M hay không.
wrong_when: A form label - a question with a particle on it reads as a chat message, not a field

marker: `bị` với người chịu ảnh hưởng làm chủ ngữ
gloss_en: `bị` marking an unwanted event, affected party as subject
what_it_carries: Says who the thing happened to, which is exactly what the English passive deletes
translated_instead: `được … bởi`, a passive Vietnamese does not have outside translated text
example_human: Có hai đơn bị trễ, cả hai đều gọi trước.
example_translated: Hai đơn hàng đã được giao trễ bởi đơn vị vận chuyển.
wrong_when: Never wrong in Vietnamese. The row exists because the passive calque arrives in its place

marker: Từ láy thay cho `rất` cộng tính từ
gloss_en: reduplication instead of a stacked intensifier
detect_regex: \b(?:từ từ|nho nhỏ|sạch sẽ|đo đỏ|xinh xinh|hơi hơi|đều đều|chầm chậm|thoang thoảng|mằn mặn|ngòn ngọt)\b
what_it_carries: Grades the quality inside the word instead of parking an adverb in front of it
translated_instead: `rất` plus an adjective, once per sentence, because the English had `very`
example_human: Nước dùng ngòn ngọt, không phải ngọt đường.
example_translated: Nước dùng có vị rất ngọt tự nhiên.
wrong_when: A measured number is available, and then the number is better

marker: Chuỗi động từ liền nhau, không liên từ
gloss_en: verbs strung directly with no connective
what_it_carries: Puts the actions in the order they happened with nothing between them
translated_instead: A subordinate clause opened by `bằng cách` or `sau khi`
example_human: Chạy qua chợ lấy rau về nấu.
example_translated: Sau khi đến chợ để mua rau, tiến hành chế biến.
wrong_when: Never wrong. It is manual because the chain has no fixed shape to match

marker: `cho` chỉ người được hưởng, nằm trong cụm động từ
what_it_carries: Names who the action is for, in the verb, where the action is
translated_instead: A `dành cho quý khách` noun phrase bolted onto the end of the sentence
example_human: Gói riêng phần đá cho dễ mang.
example_translated: Đá được đóng gói riêng nhằm thuận tiện cho quý khách.
wrong_when: Nobody benefits, and then cho is padding

marker: Số đo cụ thể ở chỗ đáng lẽ là tính từ mức độ
gloss_en: a checkable quantity where a degree adjective would go
what_it_carries: Gives the reader a number they can check, which is the one thing an adjective cannot do
translated_instead: A degree adjective - `nhanh chóng`, `đa dạng`, `chất lượng cao`
example_human: Bốn giờ sáng bắt đầu, sáu giờ mở cửa.
example_translated: Quy trình chuẩn bị được thực hiện từ sáng sớm.
wrong_when: The number is not known. Then say so, rather than inventing one to pass this row

marker: And / But / So opening a sentence
what_it_carries: Carries the previous sentence forward without reaching for a Latinate connective
translated_instead: Furthermore, Moreover, Additionally
example_human: The roast date is on the bag. And on the invoice.
example_translated: Furthermore, the roast date is indicated on both the packaging and the invoice.
wrong_when: Three sentences running, which is a tic rather than a voice

marker: Relative `that` left out
what_it_carries: The clause the way it is spoken, without the pronoun the speaker never says
translated_instead: Every relative pronoun present, because a generator never omits one
example_human: The shop you bought it from keeps the record.
example_translated: The retail location at which the purchase was made maintains the record.
wrong_when: The sentence is long enough that the reader needs the signpost

marker: Phrasal verb where a Latinate single word would fit
gloss_en: phrasal verb preferred to its Latinate synonym
detect_regex: \b(?:use up|used up|put off|find out|found out|set up|hand over|handed over|turn down|turned down|run out|ran out|take on|work out)\b
what_it_carries: The verb a person reaches for first
translated_instead: utilise, postpone, ascertain, establish, decline
example_human: Two of them ran out before noon.
example_translated: Inventory of two items was depleted prior to midday.
wrong_when: A legal or technical term is the precise one and the phrasal verb is only friendlier

marker: `got` passive rather than `was`
what_it_carries: Marks the event as something that happened to somebody, and keeps them in the sentence
translated_instead: A `was … by` passive with the affected party moved to the end or deleted
example_human: Two customers got charged twice.
example_translated: Duplicate charges were applied to two customer accounts.
wrong_when: pr; a regulatory filing, where got is too loose to stand

marker: Contracted forms
what_it_carries: The register of somebody talking rather than somebody filing
translated_instead: Every form expanded, which is the cheapest tell in English and the easiest to fix
example_human: It's on the bag. We don't print it anywhere else.
example_translated: It is printed on the packaging and is not indicated elsewhere.
wrong_when: pr; a contract, where the expanded form is the convention and not a tell

marker: Preposition left at the end of the clause
what_it_carries: Puts the preposition where speech puts it, at the end
translated_instead: A fronted `from which` or `with whom`, which nobody says out loud
example_human: That is the roaster we buy from.
example_translated: That is the roasting facility from which we procure.
wrong_when: Formal legal drafting, where the fronted form is the house convention
